script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for November 30. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
One voice among millions—does it matter?  Your vote alone rarely decides anything.  But democracy isn't about one vote deciding; it's about everyone's voice counting.

Voting without information is noise, not signal. Know what you're voting on. Research candidates and issues. An informed vote contributes more than an uninformed one. Not everyone can vote easily.  Registration, access, time off work—barriers exist.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Your vote is small individually but essential collectively.  Democracy works when people participate.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Voting Commitment - Will You Use Your Voice?.

Here's your activity: Do you vote regularly? Are you registered? Do you research before voting? Make a commitment: What will you do to ensure you're an informed, participating voter? This helps you strengthen voting as a practice.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about your voice in decisions can be applied to voting commitment - will you use your voice?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
